subsystems.name: Display module
subsystems.role: a tiny transparent screen inside one lens that floats numbers in front of the swimmer's eye without blocking the view.

subsystems.name: Goggle lens and frame
subsystems.role: keeps water out and sight clear while holding the embedded optics.

subsystems.name: Electronics pod
subsystems.role: the brains and battery, clamped to the goggle strap behind the head.

subsystems.name: Motion sensing
subsystems.role: works out strokes, laps and turns without any external equipment.

subsystems.name: Heart-rate sensing
subsystems.role: measures pulse during the swim and feeds it to the display.

subsystems.name: Firmware and companion app
subsystems.role: turns raw motion into pace, splits and stroke counts, and lets workouts be set up on a phone.

buildSteps.title: Design the optics
buildSteps.detail: Ray-tracing software is used to work out how a virtual image can be projected through a swimmer's goggle lens and appear focused a couple of metres ahead, while remaining legible against bright water.

buildSteps.title: Make the waveguide
buildSteps.detail: Fine diffraction gratings are patterned onto a master and replicated onto a thin glass or polymer sheet, which is laminated into the lens so the image travels along it and exits at the pupil.

buildSteps.title: Build the micro-display
buildSteps.detail: A chip-scale panel — a miniature organic LED array or a lit liquid-crystal panel — is mounted with its driver circuit and connected by a flexible cable.

buildSteps.title: Seal the electronics
buildSteps.detail: Chip, radio, battery and controls are potted into a housing that survives repeated immersion and chlorine or salt water.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate the sensors
buildSteps.detail: Each inertial unit is calibrated for offset and drift, and the magnetometer is corrected for the metal-rich environment of an indoor pool.

buildSteps.title: Write the swimming algorithms
buildSteps.detail: Firmware learns to count strokes, spot tumble turns and open turns, and mark manual laps from a button press.

buildSteps.title: Test in water
buildSteps.detail: Pressure testing, drop and leak testing, optical legibility checks underwater, and pool trials against a stopwatch to validate distance and pace.

buildSteps.title: Pair, update and ship
buildSteps.detail: Over-the-air firmware updates and phone pairing are validated, then units are assembled and shipped with the app.

prerequisites.why: the same optics used in augmented-reality glasses, but engineered to stay readable in bright, moving water.
the screen must be tiny, bright and efficient enough to run from a small goggle battery.
solid-state accelerometers and gyroscopes are what make stroke and lap detection possible without touching the water.
light-based pulse measurement in a strap gives the display a heart-rate figure without a chest belt of electrodes.
Bluetooth links to phone and strap, and seals must hold at repeated swim depth.

pathway.milestone: goggles that show live pace, splits and stroke data, with heart rate from a paired strap
pathway.unlocks: pool swimmers can train to a target pace without looking at a clock.

pathway.milestone: heart rate and more sensing built directly into the goggles
pathway.unlocks: one device instead of two, and fewer pairing failures.

pathway.milestone: open-water modes with audio or haptic coaching cues
pathway.unlocks: usable guidance in lakes and sea, where the swimmer cannot read a watch or clock face.

pathway.milestone: richer augmented-reality overlays and multi-swimmer training features
pathway.unlocks: virtual pacemakers, live lane data and remote coaching.
